name: multilabel_margin_loss
description: Representative ATen overload (NOT an exclusive ABI): aten::multilabel_margin_loss(Tensor self, Tensor target, int reduction=1) -> Tensor. Registered schemas, verbatim: "aten::multilabel_margin_loss(Tensor self, Tensor target, int reduction=1) -> Tensor"; "aten::multilabel_margin_loss.out(Tensor self, Tensor target, int reduction=1, *, Tensor(a!) out) -> Tensor(a!)". The original Gems pytest owns the full contract for every overload, keyword argument, return, error, aliasing and mutation behavior; tests must never be narrowed to this one representative signature and reference behavior must never be adapted to fit it. Semantics: multilabel_margin_loss scores an (N, C) float matrix, or a single rank<=1 C-class row, against an int64 target of exactly the same shape whose rows list active class ids terminated by a -1 sentinel. reduction follows at::Reduction: 0 yields the per-row losses as a (N,) tensor, 1 the mean and 2 the sum, both 0-dim scalars for this allocating overload; omitting reduction exercises the schema default 1. The native kernel accepts rank<=2 only, so the high-rank spec shapes are folded to rank 2 with the element count preserved, and broadcast is exempt because input and target must match exactly (mismatched shapes are rejected). Input-dtype negatives were probed on one measured vendor (the NVIDIA CUDA backend) and the pytest scopes that test to that vendor, gating int64 and float8 on probed capability flags; only floating input dtypes are exercised as supported in that snapshot, and non-int64 targets raise. The out overload accepts reduction positionally (reduction is positional_or_keyword in the schema) and out as a required keyword-only argument, writes into that out tensor, returns it (returns_alias_of out), mutates it, and may resize the buffer it is handed (a (1,) buffer becomes 0-dim for the scalar reductions). Those conditional, overload-specific effects are exercised by pytest and are intentionally not expressed by this single-overload model.
